h1: 137 Pillars House — a 140-year-old teak house turned luxury boutique on the Ping River
intro: Picture stepping through the gate to find a dark-brown teak house with a high pitched roof and long verandahs, more than 140 years old, standing in a quiet garden by the Ping River — 137 Pillars House is the hotel many reviews say redefined luxury in Chiang Mai. Not a glass tower, but a relic of the teak-trading era, carefully restored. A member of Small Luxury Hotels of the World, its 30 suites start from approx. THB 18,000/night.
galleryAlts: The 25-metre outdoor pool at 137 Pillars House ringed by a tall green wall of plants
Colonial-style suite with a four-poster bed, Victorian bathtub and polished teak floors
The 1880 teak building of 137 Pillars House with its verandahs and carved balustrades

body.html: The story starts in 1880, when this teak building was used as an office of the East Borneo Company, in the era when merchants harvested teak from the northern forests. Over more than a century it passed through several owners before being meticulously restored and reopened as 137 Pillars House. The name comes from the 137 teak pillars that hold up the main building — guests often enjoy walking around to count them for themselves.

All 30 rooms are suites of 70 square metres or more. Even the entry-level Rajah Brooke Suite runs to 70 sqm — larger than the Superior rooms at most 5-star hotels in Chiang Mai. Expect polished teak floors, high ceilings, four-poster beds, free-standing Victorian bathtubs, both indoor and outdoor showers, and period-correct colonial furniture, yet with thoroughly modern Wi-Fi and bathrooms. Many suites have a vintage-tiled verandah looking onto the garden — the part reviews single out as their favourite.
"Sipping tea on the private verandah first thing in the morning, birdsong around me and a faint scent of teak — I forgot I was in the middle of Chiang Mai."

The 25-metre outdoor pool is ringed by a roughly 12-metre wall of climbing greenery, giving the feel of a private pool in a secret garden. No loud music, no pool-party atmosphere. Many reviews call it the best pool in Chiang Mai for anyone who wants privacy. The spa is open daily with local Lanna herbal treatments, and the bar and library open in the evening for quiet reading or a drink.

Palette restaurant serves Thai dishes and recipes adapted from older sources. Breakfast here comes up again and again in reviews — Thai fruit, freshly baked pastries, eggs cooked to order and a made-to-order Thai set. Many guests say breakfast alone is worth half the room rate. The butler-style service appears just when you need it, without hovering — and reviews credit it as the thing that sets 137 Pillars apart from hotels that call themselves luxury but whose service is still finding its feet.

The location is in the Wat Gate district, on the east bank of the Ping River — about 10 minutes by car from the Night Bazaar and roughly 15 minutes from the Old City. It is far quieter than hotels in the centre, but that also means a Grab is needed to reach the night markets or city temples. A 9.5 from 51 reviews on Trip.com, and a top ranking among Chiang Mai hotels on TripAdvisor, are hard to argue with.

To be honest, 137 Pillars House is not for everyone. Rates start at roughly THB 18,000–22,000/night for entry-level suites and climb to about THB 45,000 for the Louis Leonowens Pool Suite. If you plan to spend most of your time out of the hotel — markets, the mountains, barely in your room — the money may not be worth it. But if the hotel is the destination of the trip, the place where you want to sit still, eat well, watch the garden and feel time slow down, it delivers that in a way few addresses in Chiang Mai can.

A tip from reading many reviews here: ask for a suite that looks directly onto the main teak building — the garden view in front of the House is the most classic angle of the hotel. In high season (November–February), book at least two months ahead, as the best rooms sell out fast.

honestSummary: 137 Pillars House is at its best for travellers who want an experience ordinary new hotels can't provide — tangible history, intuitive service and the quiet of a private residence. Just accept that the location isn't central and the price isn't for every trip.
honestChecks: If you plan to be out sightseeing from dawn to dusk every day — this becomes an expensive place to simply sleep → consider a more central hotel at a lower rate.
If you're travelling as a large family with young children — the atmosphere leans adult and quiet, and interconnecting rooms are limited → it suits couples or groups of adults better.
If high season (Nov–Feb) is approaching and you haven't booked — the good suites sell out fast, leaving only the priciest rooms → book 2+ months ahead and lock in free cancellation first.

faqTitle: Frequently Asked Questions — 137 Pillars House Chiang Mai

faq.q: Where is 137 Pillars House in Chiang Mai and what's nearby?
faq.a: 137 Pillars House is at 2 Nawatgate Road in the Wat Gate district, on the east bank of the Ping River. It's about 10 minutes by car from the Night Bazaar, 15 minutes from the Old City and 17 minutes from Chiang Mai Airport. The district is quiet, with historic temples and pretty local cafés to walk to.

faq.q: What are the starting prices and room types at 137 Pillars House?
faq.a: Rates start from approx. THB 18,000/night for the 70 sqm Rajah Brooke Suite. The largest, the Louis Leonowens Pool Suite (135 sqm, with a private pool), runs around THB 45,000. Prices depend on dates and package, so compare a few platforms before booking.

faq.q: Who is 137 Pillars House best suited for?
faq.a: It's ideal for couples, honeymoons or anyone who wants genuine rest. The atmosphere is adult and quiet rather than family-oriented, and it suits travellers who want a hotel with history and a high level of privacy rather than a large resort.

faq.q: What awards or recognition does 137 Pillars House have?
faq.a: 137 Pillars House is a member of Small Luxury Hotels of the World, has been featured in several international travel publications, ranks near the top of Chiang Mai hotels on TripAdvisor, and scores 9.5 from 51 reviews on Trip.com.

faq.q: How far ahead should I book, and is cancellation flexible?
faq.a: For high season (November–February) book 2–3 months ahead, as the hotel has only 30 rooms. Off-season, 4–6 weeks is usually enough. Every platform offers a Free Cancellation option — choose that first if your plans aren't firm.

faq.q: How good is breakfast at 137 Pillars House, and is it included?
faq.a: Breakfast at Palette restaurant is the most-praised part of the stay in reviews — Thai fruit, freshly baked bread, eggs cooked to order and a made-to-order Thai set. Some packages include breakfast, so always check at booking, as it's well worth it when bundled in.
